entries.title: A moment with your full attention
entries.summary: Both books value attention during ordinary time together. Davies acknowledges competing commitments and offers ways to turn toward a child without expecting an adult to attend to everything at once.
entries.cue: When you are together but your attention keeps moving elsewhere.
detail: The Baby authors suggest using care as time to connect, and sometimes simply holding and enjoying a baby without another purpose. These can be moments within the day you already have.

When a child wants to talk, Davies describes either pausing to listen or telling them when she can listen after finishing her task. She also sometimes writes down a distracting thought for later or puts her phone away so that she is less tempted to check it.

The Baby authors make a similar distinction about photographs: pictures can hold memories, and the adult can be in some of them, but every moment need not be recorded. These are possibilities for attention and enjoyment, not a demand to document family life.
